name: Lot
charge: A righteous man vexed with the filthy conversation of the wicked; sheltering the strangers at his door
summary: He chose the plain of Sodom and lived to regret it, but Peter calls him just Lot, vexed from day to day with the unlawful deeds of the city. He took the two strangers into his house and stood in his door against the men of the city. The angels took him by the hand and led him out before the fire fell.
offense: The obedience is genuine and the man is compromised, and the case is more useful for holding both. He chose the plain and ended sitting in the gate of Sodom as one of its men (Genesis 19:1). But when two strangers arrived he pressed them to lodge with him and fed them, and when the city surrounded the house he went outside (Genesis 19:6) and shut the door behind him rather than surrender guests he had taken in (Genesis 19:6). Peter's verdict, that he was a righteous man vexed from day to day by what he saw and heard (2 Peter 2:8), is the New Testament's reading of a life the record itself shows to be badly placed (2 Peter 2:6-9). His reception of the strangers must not conceal his offer of his two daughters to the mob (Genesis 19:8). Protecting guests did not make his daughters available for violence. The angels, not that offer, stopped the attack: they drew Lot inside and shut the door. When he warned his sons in law, they treated the warning as mockery (Genesis 19:10-14). The urgency of leaving exposed how little authority his warning carried within the city he had chosen.
judgment: He was taken out before the fire fell, and the manner of it is recorded without flattery: he lingered, and the angels took him by the hand and his wife and his daughters (Genesis 19:16) and led them out. Genesis records both the Lord's mercy in bringing him out and God's remembrance of Abraham (Genesis 19:16; Genesis 19:29). Peter draws the rule that the Lord knows how to deliver the godly out of temptations (2 Peter 2:9). Lot reached Zoar, the cities were overthrown, and his wife looked back and became a pillar of salt (Genesis 19:23-26). Deliverance preserved his life without preserving the household's life in Sodom.

entries.commentary: Lot sat in the gate and pressed the two angels into his house, because he knew the men of Sodom. He made them a feast, and they did eat; angels have bodies and functions like men.

The men of Sodom, old and young, all the people from every quarter, compassed the house and demanded the men, that we may know them. To know in scripture is to lie with: Rebekah was a virgin, neither had any man known her. The whole city, both small and great, was given to this wickedness.

Lot went out and said, I pray you, brethren, do not so wickedly. This is Genesis, way before [Leviticus 18](/bible/leviticus/18); sodomy was already wickedness and already unlawful before the law was written at Sinai. They pressed on Lot to break the door, and the angels smote them with blindness, small and great, so that they wearied themselves to find the door.

Lot's sons in law took him as one that mocked, and they perished. When the warning comes, treating it as a joke is death. While Lot lingered, the angels laid hold on his hand, the Lord being merciful to him. Then the instruction: Escape for thy life; look not behind thee; escape to the mountain.

The angel told Lot, Haste thee, for I cannot do any thing till thou be come thither. The destruction waited on the righteous being brought out, the same way the angels in [Revelation 7](/bible/revelation/7) hold the four winds until the servants of God are sealed. When Lot entered Zoar, the Lord rained brimstone and fire on Sodom and Gomorrah. Those cities are set forth for an example, suffering the vengeance of eternal fire; what was done there on a small scale is done in spiritual Sodom on a greater scale, and the example stands. Just Lot was delivered, a righteous man vexed from day to day with the filthy conversation and unlawful deeds of the wicked. A righteous man cannot be at home with that conduct.

Lot's wife looked back, against the instruction, and became a pillar of salt: a standing monument of an unbelieving soul. Remember Lot's wife: three words among the weightiest in the scriptures. As it was in the days of Lot, they ate, drank, bought, sold, planted, and builded until the day the fire fell; so shall it be in the day when the Son of man is revealed. If you find yourself reminiscing after the old life, remember Lot's wife.

Lot's daughters thought Sodom had been the whole world and no man was left on the earth to give them seed, so they made their father drink wine and lay with him; he perceived not when they lay down nor when they arose. Do not take any wayward idea from this: uncovering the nakedness of thy father is against the laws of the Most High. It was unlawful then and it is unlawful now. The firstborn bare Moab, father of the Moabites, and the younger bare Benammi, father of the Ammonites, unto this day. In this teaching those nations are identified with the peoples known today as the Chinese and the Japanese.

verses.text: And there came two angels to Sodom at even; and Lot sat in the gate of Sodom: and Lot seeing them rose up to meet them; and he bowed himself with his face toward the ground;

And he said, Behold now, my lords, turn in, I pray you, into your servant’s house, and tarry all night, and wash your feet, and ye shall rise up early, and go on your ways. And they said, Nay; but we will abide in the street all night.
And he pressed upon them greatly; and they turned in unto him, and entered into his house; and he made them a feast, and did bake unleavened bread, and they did eat.
And Lot went out at the door unto them, and shut the door after him,
And said, I pray you, brethren, do not so wickedly.

Behold now, I have two daughters which have not known man; let me, I pray you, bring them out unto you, and do ye to them as is good in your eyes: only unto these men do nothing; for therefore came they under the shadow of my roof.
And the men said unto Lot, Hast thou here any besides? son in law, and thy sons, and thy daughters, and whatsoever thou hast in the city, bring them out of this place:
For we will destroy this place, because the cry of them is waxen great before the face of the Lord; and the Lord hath sent us to destroy it.

And Lot went out, and spake unto his sons in law, which married his daughters, and said, Up, get you out of this place; for the Lord will destroy this city. But he seemed as one that mocked unto his sons in law.
And when the morning arose, then the angels hastened Lot, saying, Arise, take thy wife, and thy two daughters, which are here; lest thou be consumed in the iniquity of the city.

And while he lingered, the men laid hold upon his hand, and upon the hand of his wife, and upon the hand of his two daughters; the Lord being merciful unto him: and they brought him forth, and set him without the city.

And it came to pass, when they had brought them forth abroad, that he said, Escape for thy life; look not behind thee, neither stay thou in all the plain; escape to the mountain, lest thou be consumed.
And it came to pass, when God destroyed the cities of the plain, that God remembered Abraham, and sent Lot out of the midst of the overthrow, when he overthrew the cities in the which Lot dwelt.
And turning the cities of Sodom and Gomorrha into ashes condemned them with an overthrow, making them an ensample unto those that after should live ungodly;
And delivered just Lot, vexed with the filthy conversation of the wicked:
(For that righteous man dwelling among them, in seeing and hearing, vexed his righteous soul from day to day with their unlawful deeds;)
The Lord knoweth how to deliver the godly out of temptations, and to reserve the unjust unto the day of judgment to be punished:
Be not forgetful to entertain strangers: for thereby some have entertained angels unawares.
